text:
Connor O'Brien: Need a decision today on LTS backports for runtime-1.22.x. Which profile-pack related fixes are MUST backport vs "next minor only"? Please drop PRs + risk + QA coverage. We’re trying to keep LTS tight.

Connor O'Brien: Candidates I’ve seen:
- PR-24988 (hotfix: revert aggressive batching default -> p99 regression)
- PR-24958 (fix: prevent profile mismatch when model reloads across GPU pools)
- PR-25003 (profile-aware admission control)
- PR-25014 (/health + debug endpoint includes profile pack version)
- PR-25071 (L40S KV cache headroom tweak)

Sean Gallagher: From SRE side, anything that touches tail latency regressions or correctness should go to LTS. Observability-only can probably wait unless it’s required to triage incidents.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Our on-call pain last week was "is this pool on the new profile" and "did it pick the right kernel". The debug endpoint (PR-25014) would’ve saved time, but it’s not a functional fix.

Mateo Alvarez: Strong opinion: PR-24958 is LTS mandatory. Profile mismatch on model reload is a correctness/consistency issue and can cause unexpected perf/oom. It has a regression test.

Omar El-Sayed: Agree on 24958. For 25071 (L40S headroom): it reduces OOM risk under bursty traffic. It’s a knob change, but it's toward safety. We have benchmark-lab runs from Jan 28 showing negligible perf impact, but better stability.

Sofia Ivanova: PR-24988 (batching revert) should be LTS mandatory as well. That regression hit p99 and triggered the incident thread. It’s literally a rollback of a default.

Connor O'Brien: OK, so far "must": 24958, 24988. What about 25003? admission control is more logic.

Benji Okafor: 25003 changes behavior under overload. It’s safer in theory but higher blast radius. It also interacts with scheduler queue limits and customer traffic patterns.

Sean Gallagher: I’m nervous about backporting 25003 to LTS unless we have broad canary coverage. Overload behavior changes can cause customer-visible throughput drops / weird 429 patterns.

Sahana Iyer: QA angle:
- 24958: unit/regression test included + we can add a quick LTS CI job to run profile selection + reload loop. Low risk.
- 24988: covered by perf-canary scenarios (mixed prefill/decode), and it’s a revert. Low risk.
- 25003: needs load test coverage. Our current perf suite does NOT simulate sustained overload w/ mixed models across pools in a way I’d trust for LTS.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel side: no need to backport anything else from kernel selection for LTS. The H100 v3 kernel work is in 24911 but that's already in 1.22, right? The backport list here is more scheduler/memory.

Ethan Park: PR-25014 (/health + debug endpoint profile_version) is extremely low risk. It’s additive. Would help support (INT-8831) and customers asking to confirm pinning.

Allison Grant: If we backport 25014, I also want to ensure the label names are stable. But PR-25014 is just surfacing fields in existing endpoints; no metric changes.

Rafael Mendes: I’d vote yes on 25014 for LTS. It’s not "required", but it’s cheap and reduces MTTR.

Connor O'Brien: Noted. What about 25071 (L40S headroom)? We have SUP-21958. If we *don’t* backport, we’ll keep telling support "cap concurrency / pin older profile".

Omar El-Sayed: 25071 is a config default change (profile values). It’s safer than leaving current L40S default. Fragmentation counter data shows fewer near-OOM oscillations.

Sean Gallagher: Risk assessment for 25071: might lower max throughput slightly. But for L40S we’re already constrained; I’ll take fewer OOMs over marginal tokens/sec. If we backport, we should document in LTS notes: "L40S: increased KV cache headroom; may reduce peak concurrency by ~1-2 requests depending on workload".

Sofia Ivanova: +1 to backport 25071. OOM -> retry storms are worse than small throughput reductions.

Connor O'Brien: Ok, provisional plan:
MUST backport to runtime-1.22 LTS:
- PR-24958 (profile mismatch on model reload)
- PR-24988 (revert batching default that regressed p99)
Strongly consider:
- PR-25071 (L40S KV cache headroom safety)
Nice-to-have:
- PR-25014 (debug endpoints)
NO for LTS (next minor):
- PR-25003 (admission control) unless someone convinces me + we can gate with extra load tests

Sahana Iyer: For "strongly consider" 25071, I can run a targeted L40S stability suite on the LTS branch once it’s cherry-picked. We’ll compare OOM count + p95/p99 tokens/sec deltas against LTS baseline. Should have results tomorrow.

Mateo Alvarez: Sounds right. If we’re hesitant, we can backport 25071 behind the profile pack version pin for L40S only (so Hosted L40S gets it, Dedicated can opt-in). Not sure if that’s extra complexity though.

Ethan Park: It’s already profile-scoped; the backport is just changing default values for L40S profile. Dedicated overrides can still pin old version if needed.

Sean Gallagher: Please make sure rollback is clean: if 25071 backport causes trouble, SRE should be able to flip back to prior profile_version via existing mechanism, no code rollback.

Connor O'Brien: Ack. We’ll call out "rollback = pin profile_version" in release notes.

Allison Grant: If we do 25014, please ensure we don't leak customer identifiers in debug bundles. Keep it to `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `sku`, `driver`, `cuda`.

Connor O'Brien: Yep.

Hiro Tanaka: One more note: if 24988 is backported, ensure it also includes the config snapshot update so we don’t drift between LTS and main. :thumbsup:

Connor O'Brien: Great. Action items:
- Connor: prep cherry-picks for 24958 + 24988 today.
- Sahana: run L40S stability suite for 25071 on LTS once ready.
- Ethan: sanity-check 25014 diff for endpoint compatibility; optional backport if no objections.
- Everyone: any last-minute "must" PRs, speak now.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: from SRE. Keep LTS minimal.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup:

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup: I’ll add a one-liner to the support runbook about verifying via /health once 25014 lands (if we do it).

Connor O'Brien: Closing loop tomorrow after QA results.
